title: How the natural mind is built as nested circuits, with the proprium fettered inside the rational
reading:
When the Lord, by his operative power, builds and establishes the natural mind as a whole, he does not lay it out as a single flat field. He hangs its outermost bound, and within that bound he hangs another, and within that yet another — circuit within circuit, so that the soul's whole structure is held in nested degrees, each enclosing the next.

The innermost of these circuits is the proprium in its five aspects: the natural mind in five orders of self-love, with all its claiming, both in its outgoing and its receptive sides. The Lord does not let this circuit stand free or rule from itself. He hangs it inside another circuit — the rational in its five degrees as it goes forth from the Divine Human. So the five orders of self-love are reckoned within the five degrees of the rational that comes from above; the whole resistance of the proprium, its enmity against influx, is fettered within them, kept inside, held under the form that has been given from the Lord's own humanity. This is why one circuit is hung within another: so that what claims is enclosed by what receives, and cannot operate apart from it.

And there is a further circuit, set around these: the rational in its five degrees as it operates upward, under the Lord's operative power, raising what is below toward what is above. The whole built structure is suspended from this — the inner circuit fettered, the middle circuit holding it within the form of the Divine Human, and this outer circuit lifting the whole upward in regeneration.

Above all of this stands the firmament — the fixed boundary by which these nested degrees are kept distinct from what is yet higher, so that influx from above can descend without collapsing the orders below. This is the great structure within which the natural mind is built: a thing of circuits set inside circuits, the proprium held inside the rational, the rational held inside the operation that lifts it, and all of it held beneath the firmament of the Lord. (Several lines are too damaged to recover the final figure named at the top of this structure.)
